title: TSMC reportedly halts 16nm-and-below orders from Chinese firms
summary: TSMC has reportedly paused orders from Chinese companies for 16nm-and-below chips and told customers that supplying them now requires a prior U.S. export license or exemption under tightened U.S. semiconductor rules. The report says Chinese firms are consequently limited to older 28nm and 40nm processes and cannot obtain the high-bandwidth memory used in AI data centers. Previously TSMC could assess exemption eligibility itself; customers must now apply in advance, and the U.S. approved list includes Apple, AMD and Nvidia but no Chinese companies. TSMC said it will comply with the new rules.
